title: Hybrids · wild blood at home
blurb: Breeds founded on crosses with wild cats: the Asian leopard cat, the serval and the jungle cat, four to five generations back.

items.d: A leopard-cat hybrid from the 1960s, with rosettes, a glittering coat and a lot of energy.
A serval cross first bred in 1986: tall, long-legged and the largest domestic cat allowed in many countries.
A jungle-cat hybrid from Egypt's delta, bred in the United States as a tall, athletic shorthair.
A tabby bred in America to carry tiger stripes on a domestic body.
A Bengal and Oriental cross, 1994, bred for the spotted coat and the long Oriental leg.
A Geoffroy's cat hybrid from the 1970s, large, spotted and now very rare.
A bobtailed, polydactyl cat from Washington state, said to look like a small bobcat.
A curl-eared, bobtailed breed from the United States, with a heavy build and a gentle temper.
